pageCache.text:
Aims and Values
At The Gower School we aim for all our children to be happy, confident learners who achieve their full potential.
Aims
Our Nursery and Primary schools are built around these three core aims. Young children and babies have an engaging start in our Montessori nursery where they receive excellent care, develop independence, good habits and love of learning. Children who continue on to our independent primary school are provided a broad curriculum with excellent teaching and plenty of sports, sciences, arts, and opportunities to discover their learning passions.
Values

pageCache.pageTitle: About Us | Islington Nursery School | The Gower School
pageCache.text:
About Us
The Gower School offers a high-quality and broad curriculum in multi-age groups aimed at the development of the whole person – mind, body, heart and soul. We teach academic and social skills, as well as life skills, to last a lifetime.
The principles and philosophy of Dr Maria Montessori underpin the School’s educational approach. Montessori is widely recognised internationally as helping to educate young people to the highest modern standards and giving them a lifelong love of learning, which exceeds the expectations of the British National Curriculum.
The Gower School:
The Gower School prides itself on a high teacher-to-child ratio, far exceeding most other schools. Our teachers are all highly-trained observers. They are committed to providing each child with an individual plan of work that challenges them and which follows a steady learning programme.
Each child is allocated their own ‘Key Person’ at The Gower School. Young children make secure attachments and strong bonds with their dedicated Key Person, who takes care of them and looks out for them in their parents’ absence.
Each classroom at the school is very well-resourced, with high-quality learning materials to enable a wide range of educational learning through practical activities.
The Gower School offers a very broad curriculum – meeting and exceeding everything expected in the Early Years Foundation Stage and the National Curriculum. Activities are project-led and the children all learn core lessons and then follow their interests by researching connected topics. All our learning is very hands-on and children learn through activity in the environment. We are committed to strong partnership-working with parents and run a continuous programme of parent workshops and social events throughout the year. We fundraise regularly for charity – raising in excess of £10,000 each year – and the children are engaged in their local community.
The Gower School also prides itself on a wonderful range of specialist-taught extra-curricular activities which run each week, both during the school day and after school, including:
as well as Yoga, French, Chinese Mandarin, Cookery, Coding, Jewellery-making, and Arts and Crafts. Our standards of music, sports and modern languages are extremely high and the children achieve impressive levels, as well as participating in concerts, events and fixtures with other schools.
Our nursery and primary schools offer, in addition to the core school day, an extensive wrap-around service, incorporating a range of after-school activities and holiday-enrichment activities. These enable us to offer 8am – 6pm operating hours over 48 weeks of the year for 0-11 year-old children.
At The Gower School we take a nurturing approach to look at the whole child. We celebrate their many achievements and milestones with you as they grow and blossom into independent-minded, creative, responsible young people. We are a school which values the individuality of each child. We pride ourselves on meeting each child’s needs to ensure they are happy, stimulated and able to be themselves.
Thank you for your interest in The Gower School.
Dance (ballet, modern dance, theatre)

pageCache.pageTitle: Prinicpal's Welcome | Independent School | The Gower School
pageCache.text:
Principal’s Welcome
“Welcome to The Gower School, which I founded in 2000.
Our independent school’s work was once again rated as Outstanding and Excellent in every category following our most recent external inspection. We offer a broad curriculum in multi-age classrooms which aims to develop the whole person – their mind, body, heart and soul. We teach academic, social and other valuable skills to last a lifetime. Our goal is to make sure that our girls and boys are confident, happy all-rounders with a love of learning.
We are guided not by bureaucratic edict but by the Montessori philosophy of education that espouses respect for the individual child, nurturing their surroundings and self-reliance. We also believe in purposeful and fulfilling activities that break down the artificial division of ‘work’ and ‘play’. Our experience is that reinforcing the inner drive for self-improvement is more effective in academic attainment and developing the whole child, than promoting peer-competitiveness.
The warm, friendly atmosphere is immediately apparent when you enter our school. It is a unique environment where everybody gets to know every child and family by name. It is important to me that every child is recognised as an individual. Our very high ratio of teachers to children ensures we can nurture their talents and give them the specific help that they need to succeed.
Our staff are fun, inspirational people and are specialists in the age group or developmental stage they work with. They are keen observers and facilitators who recognise varying learning styles, helping not doing and coaching, not lecturing. Many staff have committed years of service to our school. They believe passionately in the development of the individual child, not moulding or stuffing them with data.
I am proud to create such an exciting place for a child to grow and learn. Our extensive extra-curricular programme and flexible approach respond to children’s interests through broad projects. The Gower School is large enough to provide a full range of facilities and attract a loyal and highly capable staff. Our community also retains personal touches and fosters independence of mind, curiosity and self-confidence. Kindness, good manners and consideration of others are TGS essentials.
We are proud to call Islington our home and be part of a diverse community of parents, students and staff. We fully take advantage of all the best central London offers on our doorstep.
At The Gower School, we are all working towards a shared vision, held together by common-sense educational values. Being Principal is an incredible experience. It is wonderful to be a part of our amazing children’s journey through their early years and primary education as they become little people. I look forward to welcoming you to our school.”
Emma Gowers, Principal

French
At The Gower School, we teach French from the Nursery school upwards when the children reach two and a half years old. Our Primary School children have a lesson every week in small groups for the younger children, and take on written French and grammar in the Upper School (from Form Three upwards).
There are After School Clubs for French, including one for native speakers.

pageCache.pageTitle: Geography and History | Primary School Curriculum | The Gower School
pageCache.text:
Geography and History
Throughout the school, the teaching of History and Geography is very much cross-curricular – starting in Lower School (Reception to Form Two) with the Creation of the Universe, the development of Animal Life (early man) and the History of Writing. In Upper School, the topics studied include The Active Planet, The Environment, The Stone Age, The Vikings, The Victorians and the World Wars. We also place a special emphasis on our place in our immediate environment by looking at the development of London through time.
Geography is a foundation subject, and as a Montessori school, we place great emphasis on the world around us. The subject encourages pupils to acquire and develop both the skills and the knowledge necessary to understand the world in which we live.
The teaching of History allows the children to develop empathy and critical thinking as well as learning about the past. A variety of techniques are used to teach the subject including primary and secondary source material, ICT, films and field trips to sites of historical significance.
Through the teaching of both subjects, we aim to give the children a sense of place in the world.
Explore Open Mornings & Visits

pageCache.pageTitle: PSHEE & Citizenship | Primary School Curriculum | The Gower School
pageCache.text:
PSHEE & Citizenship
Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education and Citizenship is embedded in our curriculum at The Gower School. We believe we have a responsibility to ensure that the information our children receive is grounded in the context of accepted values, based on sound moral principles.
PSHEE is a fun, exciting and essential element to all of the teaching and learning that takes place here. This important and thought provoking subject is at the core of enhancing personal development and well-being and establishing a safe learning environment for all children. We believe this enables them to learn more effectively.
We promote the use of good manners and social skills and children are encouraged to think openly about the world that they live in and their contribution to their local community.
Children undertake many life-skills activities which have both direct and indirect aims, such as refining hand muscles for writing, extending concentration or working from left to right in reading and writing.
Our Special Helper system offers each child the opportunity to help their teacher and enjoy an extra special day at school. Activities such as bringing in a favourite CD, setting up the snack area, reading to younger children, taking the register and running errands all contribute to the growth of self-esteem and independence.
Each class has a separate weekly PSHEE lesson and the topics covered include:
Children often share what they have learnt through displays and class assemblies.
Friendships
Food and nutrition
Well-being and emotional health
Caring for the environment

pageCache.pageTitle: Drama | Montessori School Curriculum | The Gower School
pageCache.text:
Drama
Drama is very much taught in a cross curricular way at The Gower School. Children engage in drama activities from Reception age by participating in plays, musicals, performances and class presentations.
Each Autumn Term each class performs a play at the Platform Theatre in Islington for their parents and relatives. In the classroom, the children learn to work as part of a community whilst honing their own performance skills. They take pride in these plays and for many it is their highlight of the school year. In addition, several Drama, Musicals and Theatre clubs are offered for children after school. Finally, classes regularly attend several London theatre to watch live musicals or plays.
Children from Lower School onwards are offered specialised teaching from our peripatetic LAMDA qualified teachers. Children work through stages of this drama curriculum and prepare for yearly drama exams. Beginning in Upper School, children can participate in the ISA Shakespeare Monologue Competition, where they memorise and film themselves performing one of Shakespeare’s plays.
Explore Open Mornings & Visits

pageCache.pageTitle: Music | Montessori School Curriculum | The Gower School
pageCache.text:
Music
Every child at our primary school has a weekly singing/percussion/music appreciation lesson with our experienced music teacher, Miss Wilkinson. All our children’s music learning is linked to the London Symphony Orchestra’s education programme and our children attend at least two concerts a year at the Barbican.
From Form One, every child learns to play the recorder in small groups with a specialist recorder teacher, Miss Widdup, and there is also a Recorder Ensemble. There are two popular Choirs for the Lower and Upper School. In addition, there are a range of teachers who visit to teach private instrumental or voice lessons each week. Individual music lessons are offered for a variety of instruments such as piano, violin, guitar and the voice.
We are very proud of the fact that our children perform in recitals and concerts for the elderly in the community, in addition to class plays and assemblies. There is also an annual Music Festival at The Gower School.
We pride ourselves on our rich cultural offerings for children and we believe this makes us unique among our peers. Other musical activities offered include:
end-of-term whole school concerts twice a year.
recitals for instrumentalists.
annual Music Festival and Music Week.

pageCache.pageTitle: Prepare your child for Senior School | Exams and Interviews
pageCache.text:
Senior School Preparation Programme
Here at The Gower School, we have an in-depth knowledge of the senior school landscape – in London and further afield.
We are proud to use our years of experience to help each family identify senior schools where their child can flourish and thrive in their teenage years. You will receive advice on assessment formats and preparation, as well as emotional support for the child throughout the process. We will make this journey as smooth as possible, and offer help and guidance every step of the way.
Senior School Exam and Interview Preparation
Our programme is tailored to your family. We understand that every child is unique, and has different strengths and abilities. That is why we take an individualised approach when helping children find their perfect senior school, and prepare for exams, interviews and auditions.
Our programme is comparable to the services offered by private consultancies. However, the support we offer benefits from years of knowing your child as an individual and understanding their needs, and our ability to fully integrate their exam preparation into their learning at school.
11+ Senior School Destinations
Each year, TGS children gain entry to both selective state and independent schools – Camden School for Girls, Channing, City of London School, City of London School for Girls, Collège Français Bilingue de Londres, Dame Alice Owen, Dulwich College, Forest School, Francis Holland, Haberdashers’ Aske’s School for Girls, Henrietta Barnett, Highgate, Maida Vale, Merchant Taylors’ School, North Bridge House School, North London Collegiate School, Portland Place, Queen’s College, Regents Park, South Hampstead High School, St Albans High School for Girls, St Marylebone CE School Wetherby Senior, St Mary Magdalene Academy and University College School.
For a full list of senior school places offered to our current Form Six children following their recent 11+ exams, please click here.
‘The Gower School carefully guides parents through the secondary school process, starting from Form Four. You can be assured that Miss Gowers and Miss Falloon have in-depth knowledge of the application process, exams and interviews across a range of outstanding North London private and grammar schools. Our daughter got offers from most top tier schools we applied for, and got into her first choice school.’

pageCache.pageTitle: Art and Design | Primary Curriculum | The Gower School
pageCache.text:
Art and Design
Creative development is vital for a balanced education, and Art and Design help stimulate creativity and imagination. Children become involved in shaping their environment through related activities and learn to make informed judgements, as well as aesthetic and practical decisions. The Gower School encourages children to foster, enjoy and appreciate the visual arts along with a good knowledge of artists, craftspeople and designers.
Each half term, in each form group, a different artist and genre is explored in The Gower School Primary classes, and children learn the skills and techniques associated with each one. We have a dedicated Head of Art to lead art classes in Forms One through Six. Our visual art is celebrated on our social media channels, particularly on our Instagram (@thegowerschoolart). There is also an annual art Exhibition Evening at the school which parents love to attend.
Our children often enter art competitions and have been successful on many occasions, such as at the City of London School for Girls’ creativity competitions and the SATIPS Art Show. Each year, we enter the Independent Schools Association Art Competition and we consistently place in several categories, including sending pieces to the National Competition in both 2018, 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025.

pageCache.pageTitle: English | Nursery School Islington | The Gower School
pageCache.text:
English
English is central to the entire curriculum and key to all learning. It is through speaking, listening, reading and writing that children learn to understand the world in which they live. Therefore, teaching English is paramount at The Gower School. We aim to foster and develop each child’s ability to communicate effectively in oral and written contexts, with confidence and flair.
Reading and spelling are taught through a wide variety of phonetically-based Montessori materials in the Lower School and more abstract methods are used in the Upper School.
Writing and reading are an integral part of the school day. We encourage both creative writing and poetry writing, and each year our Form 5/6 children publish their poetry in a book. Our children also enter creative writing competitions, and several have won these and seen their work published.
Grammar, spelling and comprehension are taught separately throughout the school.
Recent English language teaching-related events have included:
The Gower School also organises annual events such as World Book Day, Poetry Recitation Week, Public Speech Writing/Making and a special ‘Meet the Author’ week to maintain the children’s interest and involvement in English language.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maths | Primary School Curriculum | The Gower School
pageCache.text:
Maths
At The Gower School, all our children learn in a concrete, hands-on way before moving on to more abstract concepts. All the core elements of the National Curriculum Numeracy Strategy, including mental strategies, problem solving and investigation are covered and exceeded. In addition, our independent status enables us to bring Montessori methods into our teaching.
Pupils will be able to think individually in applied and abstract ways and should progress from counting reliably to calculating fluently with all four maths operations. In Upper School (Forms Three to Six) this will be extended to include decimals, fractions, percentages, measurements, geometry, data handling, probability and simple algebra, as well as problem-solving operations which steadily increase in difficulty.
The amount of mathematics in everyday use is extensive and often cross-curricular. It is taught individually or in small groups and is all child-focused, providing us with the opportunity to differentiate extensively. We also hold an annual Maths Day with a visiting company which specialises in teaching problem-solving.
Explore Open Mornings & Visits

pageCache.pageTitle: Science | Primary School Curriculum | The Gower School
pageCache.text:
Science
At The Gower School, science is given prominence, as emphasised by the National Curriculum. The school has a dedicated Science/Arts facility which is very well-equipped – enabling children to conduct experiments, practical observations and problem-solving activities. This area includes Biology, Zoology and Biodiversity.
To keep our children really motivated and with a love for science, we also offer:
a ‘Scientist of the Week’ award.

Pre-School Fun Club
Does your nursery close during summer, and you’re left scratching your head over childcare?
Looking for fun children’s activities this summer?
The Gower School’s Pre-School Summer Club is the answer!
The Gower School Nursery offers an exciting Pre-School Summer Club for young children aged 2-5 years old. It is a great opportunity to experience our nursery and have loads of creative fun!
Children are invited to join us in the half-terms, holidays and the summer for full days of fun at our accredited Montessori nursery. Themed activities will include arts and crafts, messy play, outdoor play, music, cookery, Montessori learning, and Forest School. Our variety of activities guarantees there is always something for each child to enjoy. All sessions will take place at our Nursery site at 18 North Road, in person. We look forward to welcoming your child to a week of fun!

pageCache.pageTitle: Les Écureuils – Mixed-Age Toddlers | The Gower School
pageCache.text:
Les Écureuils – Mixed-Age Toddlers
At The Gower School’s private nursery in Islington, children are welcomed into Les Écureuils (The Little Squirrels) between the ages of two and three and a half. They are fully-equipped Montessori classrooms and are run by an excellent team of teachers. Les Écureuils is run by Mrs Denisa, who has been working with us since April 2026.
Children learn at their own pace with complete freedom to move around the classroom. They choose from a full range of stimulating activities catering to their developmental needs, in line with the Early Years Foundation Stage guidelines.
In addition to the ever-popular Home and Book Corners, Les Écureuils’ classrooms are split into five main areas in keeping with the Montessori philosophy: Practical Life, Sensorial, Language, Mathematics, and Understanding the World. The Montessori activities on offer range from simple pouring and transferring exercises to early maths and language materials. The children are shown how to roll and unroll table and floor mats and learn that this is where they carry out their activities, creating a sense of their own workspace.
In these rooms, there is a strong, age-appropriate, emphasis on the Practical Life area. This area underpins the focus on developing the children’s independence, concentration, socialisation, confidence and self-discipline. The implementation of the special helper scheme in this classroom means that the children have a free choice of snacks at any time in the morning. Preparing their own snacks and helping to serve their friends at mealtimes helps to build the child’s sense of responsibility. Independence and confidence developed through using the materials are transferred into the “real world”.
In keeping with the philosophy of the learning following the child, it is only if the child shows an inclination towards letters and numbers that these will be explored. The preparation for this is done so that when they are ready, they have the underlying strengths needed to flourish.
In the mornings, the children participate in the Montessori Work Cycle. The focus is on the teachers observing the children using the various materials on the shelf and presenting new materials/activities planned for, or in response to, their interests.
They also enjoy music and PE lessons on specific days. In the afternoons, children enjoy a range of activities from French (with a native French teacher) to music with Louise Loft, where movement, singing and playing the guitar are explored. Regular sessions of yoga with their teachers (who are all qualified in Yoga for Children), and sports skill sessions (with our PE Teacher Mr Bishop) all complement weekly music lessons with Sarah Wilkinson, our music specialist. Les Écureuils also enjoy our very popular Forest School sessions throughout the year.
Children love creative activities, so we also incorporate lots of free and messy play into the afternoons because children need that just as much as structured play! As a result, our display of artwork on the school walls is updated frequently.
In order to follow your child’s progress, weekly updates on My Montessori Child are available for each child, in addition to daily verbal feedback from your child’s Key Person when you collect your child. We produce annual written reports on your child and offer you the chance to talk to their Key Person in depth at regular one-to-one sessions to discuss their progress. The Principal will also email all parents a fortnightly nursery newsletter and send an annual report on your child’s progress.
The Gower School is also very proud to offer parents ‘My Montessori Child’ – a bespoke secure record-keeping system for Montessori schools. We use this in our nursery and Primary School and parents are able to log into our system securely to see their child’s progress.
Les Écureuils’ day runs from 8am to 6pm.
